note: Vanuatu, read on the Department of Immigration and Passport Services' own pages (immigration.gov.vu: the Employment visa, the Short-term employment visa and the Permanent residency visa, in the site's redesigned pages, and its Work in Vanuatu page) on 2026-10-30; fees are in vatu. The Employment visa is for skilled work of more than two months on an acceptable employer's sponsorship: VUV 257,500, valid 12 months with multiple entry; its holder may take no employment but that on which the visa was granted and must remain an employee of the business on which it was granted, with permission to work under the Labour (Work Permit) Act [CAP 187] (work for the sponsor). The Short-term employment visa is for sponsored skilled work of at most six months: VUV 51,500, valid '1 to 4 months' (a range the form can't hold as a term, so no term is kept), under the same conditions (work for the sponsor). Neither page says whether the visa is applied for from abroad or in Vanuatu (the Development Support visa's says 'outside Vanuatu', not these), so where to apply is left out; neither says it is renewable. The Permanent residency visa's Part A, subclass 131, is for those of Ni-Vanuatu descent and for 'people who have lived in Vanuatu for the last 12 months', applied for to the Director's office; its fee varies ('contact Vanuatu Immigration for the current fee'), and the page says nothing of the work it allows or of where its applicant must be, so only its name is kept; whether 12 months on an employment visa lead to it isn't written as years to permanence (the PR Directive Notice No. 2 of 2023 it cites wasn't read). Part B (subclasses 132 to 135) is for serious investors. The Department answers enquiries only after 30 working days of a permit's lodgment and 21 for a visa application, which isn't a decision time, so none is kept; naturalisation isn't on these pages.

sources.title: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services, Employment visa
sources.said: For skilled workers sponsored by an employer in Vanuatu for a period of more than two months. ... Validity, with multiple entry ... VUV 257,500 ... Application fee ... You do not take part in other employment, commercial or business activities, unless they are the basis on which the visa was granted. ... The main applicant remains an employee of the business in Vanuatu on which the visa was granted, with permission to work under the Labour (Work Permit) Act [CAP 187].

sources.title: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services, Short-term employment visa
sources.said: For workers sponsored by an employer in Vanuatu for skilled work of up to six months. ... 1 to 4 months ... VUV 51,500 ... The applicant must not work for more than 6 months. ... The main applicant remains an employee of the business in Vanuatu on which the visa was granted, with permission to work under the Labour (Work Permit) Act [CAP 187].

sources.title: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services, Work In Vanuatu
sources.said: The Employment Visa is valid for 12 months and is allowed for multiple entry. ... The visa application charge for an Employment visa is 257,500 vatu

sources.title: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services, Permanent residency visa
sources.said: Part A, subclass 131, is for people whose parents are Ni-Vanuatu or of Ni-Vanuatu descent, and for people who have lived in Vanuatu for the last 12 months. ... Fees vary by category and requirements, so contact Vanuatu Immigration for the current fee.

sources.title: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services, Variation In Application Processing Timeline
sources.said: Please note that the department will only respond to enquiries after 30 working days of Permit lodgment, 21 working days for Visa Application and 60 days for all Citizenship application.
